reason: Reproduced every number by driving master.html cold, on BOTH grounds, no contrived starting scroll (pane.scrollTop starts at 0 in every run). At 1440x960 owner-editing the edited row's .b-copy sits at pane-relative top 445, height 79, free = clientHeight 664 - 16 = 648. One press of 'Move a week later' targets top 445 + 7 x 18px = 571, bottom 650 - exactly TWO pixels past the band. keepInBand (render-b.js:846) then computes delta = round(571 - max(16, (648-79)/2)) = 287 and applies it to pane.scrollTop in one assignment: sampled every rAF for 25 frames the trace is 0,287,287,287,... while the row's own .b-item top transitions over 0.22s. Post-press the row's pane-relative top is 284 - the moment told to go a week LATER ends 161px HIGHER on screen than it started. Jump sequence over eight presses, identical on paper and ink: 1440 = 287,0,0,384,0,0,372,0; 1280x900 = 317,0,258,0,0,378,0,252; 1152x800 = 0,258,0,252,0,252,0,252. The seat's figures match to the pixel. .b-origin ('Today, 16 July') lives inside the scrolling measure and is on screen before the first press (pane-relative top ~31); after press one it is at -25 and it is outside .b-plan's box after 8/8 presses at every desk width on both grounds - eight presses never bring it back. The four refutation lines all fail. (a) Re-centring is not correct here: the row overflowed by 2px and the correction was 287 - a 143x over-shoot that inverts the direction of the user's own action. (b) No contrived scroll: cold mount, scrollTop 0. (c) The row does stay in view, which is precisely why this is a taste defect rather than a correctness one - nothing is lost except the reader's place, the six other rows and the origin mark, all snapped instantly beneath the one thing in the product that animates. (d) 'Moves nothing else' cannot be read as a claim about the measure only: the origin, the rail and every other row are inside the same pane, so the pane IS the plan. Not covered by the gates: interaction-check.mjs runs its band loop (lines 1093-1106) only at 390 and 768, where .b-edit computes position:fixed and paneScrolls is false - I measured the 390 path and it behaves as the seat says (row moves +98px down, scrollTop stays 0, free = 1404), so the desk pane branch never executes under any standing assertion. Nothing in SETTLED.md covers it: the two prior keepInBand entries concern its EARLY RETURN on the owner-flight rail, a different branch.
sharpenedFix: Take the seat's approach - in keepInBand replace the unconditional re-centre with a minimum correction that restores the row to the band plus a small margin (pad ~24px), re-centring only in the genuine fallback where height + 2*pad exceeds free. That turns the 1440 first press into ~26px and the 1280 one into ~86px, leaves the fixed/docked path at 390 and 768 untouched (both standing band assertions still hold, now with air rather than flush), and makes the pane's motion proportional to the row's. Two sharpenings on the way it is shipped. First, if the correction is to stop reading as a snap it should share the row's own timing rather than being a bare scrollTop assignment applied in the same rAF: scroll the pane with the same 0.22s easing the .b-item top transition uses (respecting prefers-reduced-motion), so the plan follows the moment instead of teleporting under it. Second, the proposed red-green assertion needs one clause rewritten before it is written to fail: (b) - the change in pane.scrollTop is never greater than the row's own travel, 7 x Number(.b-measure[data-px]) - is the real invariant and should be asserted after every press at 1152/1279/1280/1440; but (a), that .b-origin still intersects .b-plan after all eight presses, is not satisfiable by minimum correction and should not be asserted as written. The row genuinely travels 126px per press in a 664px pane, so after roughly five presses the origin has legitimately scrolled out of the content above it. Assert instead that the origin survives the FIRST press (the case where the row overflowed by two pixels), and that it leaves only once the row can no longer share the pane with it.
